fatal_errors: The hypothesis substitutes refractory high-entropy alloys for the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 transition-metal–phosphorus alloy.
It confuses high-temperature oxidation resistance with glass-forming ability; formation of a protective surface oxide does not establish suppression of bulk crystallization.
The proposed Al, Cr, and Si additions do not reconstruct the target intervention of adjusting Fe/Co/Mn ratios, reducing P to 15 at.%, and applying rapid melt spinning.
The cited evidence supports protective oxide-film formation and oxidation resistance, not amorphization or glass-forming ability.
The falsification experiment measures oxidation kinetics rather than amorphous fraction, crystallization behavior, elemental partitioning, or critical cooling conditions.
explanation: The generated hypothesis addresses a different alloy family, intervention, and physical phenomenon. The target study found that compositional adjustment toward eutectic-dominated solidification, combined with rapid quenching at 40 m/s, suppressed segregation and phosphide nucleation and produced a fully amorphous approximately 20 μm ribbon. By contrast, the response proposes Al/Cr/Si-induced protective oxidation films in RHEAs. Its evidence only supports improved oxidation resistance, so the claimed enhancement of glass-forming ability is an unsupported extrapolation. The generic prediction of enhanced glass-forming ability provides only superficial outcome overlap and no agreement on the demonstrated material, mechanism, processing boundary, or measurements.
